findings.problem: The new guard picks the highest-semver claude-hud cache directory first, then exits 0 if that directory lacks dist/index.js. The cited upstream launcher (jarrodwatts/claude-hud@75683c6 scripts/statusline.mjs:30-39, re-read in this review) instead selects the newest version whose entry exists. So when a complete older version sits beside an incomplete newer directory (e.g. an interrupted update), the template renders nothing while upstream renders the older version. The regression test covers only absent, missing-entry and single-installed cases, and the decision says the template 'adopts' upstream's check. The guard does correctly close the old fallback that ran the project's own dist/index.js.
findings.fix: Filter candidate directories on '[ -f "<dir>dist/index.js" ]' before the sort/tail, keeping the fail-closed 'exit 0' when no candidate remains, and add a subtest with 0.10.0 missing its entry beside a complete 0.9.x. Alternatively, reword decision lines 74-76 to describe a narrower fail-closed guard.
